summary: The first step has a one-line answer already recorded in the repo: odd greedy never terminates within three terms for 4/n, n odd, because n(xy+yz+zx)=4xyz forces an even denominator (parity; greedy_algorithm_dynamics.md §1). The alt step (signature-0079, min offset k with 4/p−1/(⌈p/4⌉+k) a 2-term sum) is exactly J(p)=(a_min−3)/4 of Prop B.2 there, with its distribution to 3·10^5 (§4) and the window census to 10^8 (POINTWISE_SIZE §8). The existence-vs-algorithm caution is Theorem M/C (B1).

Checked whether the six U(n) sporadics {105, 2961, 3985, 25305, 111969, 978145} fit an RS-type 'sporadic set' pattern; FOREST_INVERSE.md §3.4 (CERTIFIED to 10^8/10^9) already settles it. All six are composites divisible by 3 or 5. U holds at every prime ≤ 10^9 and at every composite coprime to 105, and the sporadics are explained there as a 'loaded lottery': a prime q | n removes the coprime lines q | v, and the least QNR is enriched (r(n) ∈ {11,11,13,13,17,37}). This is not a finite-index sub-orbit phenomenon (U is not known to be an RS orbit: ES_APPROACH_GENERATORS §1), so the RS comparison adds nothing beyond z36_reciprocity_obstruction_home.md.

The requested factor/character pattern of the U(n) sporadics is already computed and certified in FOREST_INVERSE.md §3.4 (factorisations, n mod 24, least QNR r(n), nearest-square distance, 436 U_cop failures ≤ 10^8 all divisible by 3 or 5, none coprime to 105, U holds at all primes ≤ 10^9). So the U sporadic set is a composite small-prime-factor artefact, not a structured reciprocity family. The contrast with Ramanujan's 2719 holds only at the level of shape: Ono–Soundararajan's exceptions come from weight-3/2 L-values/GRH, while the U list is about lost lines at composite n. For ES itself the relevant sporadic set over primes is empty to 10^9.

The first step (measure the dependency structure of ES events at fixed p and compare with Erdős–Tetali/Janson hypotheses) was already done in s9_janson_dependency.md (scripts/s9_janson.c, 108 283 primes ≤ 3·10^6). Word-level Δ/μ = 3.6→9.4 and μ²/2Δ = 0.85→1.82 ≪ log p. The near-independent units are levels, with expected count only (0.44→0.97)·log p, i.e. exactly critical for the >log n exponent that the Erdős–Tetali union bound needs. s9_lower_tail_literature.md already records the decisive difference: Erdős–Tetali chooses the random set, while ES's set is fixed. The alt step (Poisson c·log²p fit) is the FRONTIER §2.4 zero-law measurement.

Logic/literature check. Erdős–Fuchs needs a representation function of the form r_{A+A} (generating function f(z)² for a 0/1 series f). ES's R(n) has generating series Σ_{t,u,v} q^{tuv−u−v} (METAPLECTIC_ES Thm K), which is not of that form, so the theorem does not apply. The natural fluctuation statement for Σ_{n≤N} R(n) is a Hardy/Voronoi-type Ω-bound for divisor sums D_{4C}^−(4Cn+1) in progressions, which is a statement about averages with no pointwise content. Erdős–Turán's direction (coverage ⇒ unbounded multiplicity) is the converse of what ES needs and is already known for ES via Linnik (FRONTIER §2.2, Prop 3.1: R(p) ≥ exp(c log p/log log p) infinitely often).

The requested enumeration (natural finite ES-like sets S_p with windmill-type involutions, parity of |S_p| over p and over all n) is the content of WINDMILL.md §3 (~7000 weights on primes) and invol_windmill_signature.md §4. E1–E3 do GF(2) span tests of 288–385 natural weighted counts against divisor-type and 1564 binary-form parity vectors for n ≤ 2·10^4; E4 uses the always-odd set X(p) = {p = uvt−u−v}, PROVED odd for prime p ≥ 5, but its odd point (p+2,1,1) is not an ES certificate. The only divisor-type parity found is the trivial TI&x=y count, and the 'transpose-only' verdict quoted in the item is that memo's own result. No new set suggested itself within the time box that is not in the tested span.

I computed Δ_m(N) = max_a #{d|N : d ≡ a (mod m)} for N = 4Cp+1, m = 4C, C ∈ {1,2,3,5,6,10,15,30}, using 298 primes p ≡ 1 (24) near 10^7 and 300 composite controls n ≡ 1 (24). The maximising class is the trivial class 1 in 94–100% of cases, because d ≡ 1 and N/d ≡ 1 pair up and 1, N are always in it. Δ/τ and P(D^−>0) are indistinguishable between primes and controls (e.g. C=1: 0.729/0.557 vs 0.720/0.567). The max-class concentration function therefore carries no information about the ES class −1. The FKT random-divisor-walk methods address interval concentration, and the class analogue reduces to the already-studied one-class lottery D^−.
